description: QLoRA (Quantized LoRA) adapters — LoRA trained on top of a base quantized to 4-bit (NF4) with paged optimizers, so a large base fine-tunes on commodity / single-GPU hardware. A registry of QLoRA SPECS (quantization + adapter shape + footprint + intent), not weights; pointers, never truth. The cost-down tier of lora_adapters: same task lift at a fraction of the VRAM. Records are synthetic/public metadata only.

adapters.name: 7B instruct QLoRA (4-bit NF4)
adapters.when_to_use: fine-tune a 7B on a single consumer GPU; the default cost-down adapter tier
adapters.tradeoff: tiny quality delta vs fp16 LoRA for most tasks; verify on the held-out set before promotion

adapters.name: 13B domain QLoRA (4-bit NF4)
adapters.when_to_use: a 13B domain adapter where a 7B under-fits but full fine-tune is unaffordable
adapters.tradeoff: more target modules = more capacity, more VRAM; output still passes the verification rail

adapters.name: Reasoning QLoRA (4-bit NF4)
adapters.when_to_use: the cheap model-side enforcer for chain_of_thought_contracts — trains the required CoT structure into a small base
adapters.tradeoff: pair with a deterministic contract gate; the adapter biases toward the structure, the gate guarantees it

adapters.name: Function-calling QLoRA (4-bit NF4)
adapters.when_to_use: reliable tool-call JSON from a small quantized base; the cheapest rung of the tool-use ladder
adapters.tradeoff: schema-validate downstream; the adapter raises the hit-rate, the validator enforces correctness

adapters.name: Edge 3B QLoRA (4-bit NF4)
adapters.when_to_use: on-device / batch-CPU narrow tasks where latency + cost dominate and scope is bounded
adapters.tradeoff: small base needs a narrow task + a deterministic harness around it (small-models-need-narrow-scope)
